## Why This Is Asked
Explores practical edge feature economics with privacy implications, not just technical feasibility.

## Key Concepts
- On-device ML cost modeling
- Privacy and compliant telemetry design
- Rollout strategy and break-even assessment

## Code Example
```javascript
function annualCost(cacheMB, cpuPct, energyJ) {
  return cacheMB * 0.2 + cpuPct * 3 + energyJ * 0.01;
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would results change if model size doubled?
- How would you validate caption latency against user tolerance?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to plan ROI for a data-driven feature, balancing cost and user value, with beginner-friendly data and timing considerations.

## Key Concepts
- ROI modeling and payback
- Data sourcing costs and API limits
- Storage and compute budgeting
- Validation and lightweight experimentation
- Privacy and governance

## Code Example
```javascript
// Simple break-even calculator
function breakEvenDays(cost, upliftPerUserPerDay, dailyActiveUsers) {
  const dailyGain = upliftPerUserPerDay * dailyActiveUsers;
  return dailyGain > 0 ? cost / dailyGain : Infinity;
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you estimate the uplift values without a full launch?
- What would be your MVP scope and validation plan?

Tests ability to design an on-device ML feature with privacy, latency, and budget constraints, plus a clear go/no-go decision after a year.

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical capabilities for designing, cost‑estimating, and validating a federated learning deployment at scale in automotive context, including privacy guarantees and unreliable connectivity.

## Key Concepts
- Federated learning with differential privacy
- Secure aggregation and encrypted model deltas
- Edge compute energy and memory budgeting
- OTA bandwidth planning and variance
- Model drift, validation, and rollback strategies
- Privacy/compliance costs and governance
- Rollout sequencing and go/no-go criteria

## Code Example
```javascript
// Pseudocode: rough OA cost model for a single vehicle
function estimateAnnualCost(modelSizeMB, energyPerUpdateJ, bandwidthPerUpdateMB, dpOverhead) {
  const updatesPerYear = 365; // conservative
  const energy = energyPerUpdateJ * updatesPerYear;
  const bandwidth = bandwidthPerUpdateMB * updatesPerYear;
  const cost = (energy * 0.0002) + (bandwidth * 0.01) + dpOverhead;
  return cost;
}
``` 

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you validate the privacy guarantees under regulatory constraints across regions?
- What monitoring metrics would you instrument to detect drift and rollback needs in production?

## Why This Is Asked
This angle tests privacy-by-design, on-device processing, and practical CBA framing for a calendar sync feature.

- On-device processing
- Conflict resolution for calendar events
- Delta-based sync and batching
- Privacy/compliance and opt-in
- Rollout cohorts and break-even analysis

```javascript
function breakevenMonths(fixedCost, netMonthlyLiftPerUser, usersPerMonth) {
  const net = netMonthlyLiftPerUser;
  if (net <= 0) return Infinity;
```

- What privacy controls would you expose to users?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design a practical 18-month CBA for on-device ML with privacy, performance, and compliance trade-offs; requires concrete numbers and policy considerations.

## Key Concepts

- On-device ML tradeoffs: model size, quantization, latency, energy
- Data minimization and privacy/compliance
- Rollout strategy, telemetry design, and break-even planning
- Drift management and rollback

## Code Example

```javascript
function energyPerImage(ms, powerMw) { return (powerMw * ms) / 1000; }
function storagePerUser(cacheMb, users) { return cacheMb * users; }
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you monitor model drift and schedule retraining for edge models?
- How would you measure FP/TP in production and adjust thresholds safely?

## Why This Is Asked

Explore a new, hands-on CBA angle focused on device-to-device comms, privacy, and energy—not common in standard server-based features.

## Key Concepts

- Local-first design and BLE energy modeling
- End-to-end encryption overhead (AES-GCM, ECDH)
- Per-message storage, latency targets for nearby delivery
- Optional cloud relay for archival and its cost, privacy implications
- Onboarding friction, rollout strategy, maintenance and drift

## Code Example

```javascript
async function encryptPayload(key, plaintext){
  const iv = crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(12));
  const enc = await crypto.subtle.encrypt({name:'AES-GCM', iv}, key, plaintext);
  return { iv: Array.from(iv), ciphertext: Array.from(new Uint8Array(enc)) };
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you estimate BLE energy for scaling to N devices?
- What metrics would you monitor post-launch and why?
- How would consent be presented and stored across devices?
- What edge cases break the CBA assumptions (e.g., busy networks, OS sleep)?
